what_is_included_vs_extra.point: At Alert Labs the subscription buys analytics, alerts, dashboards, automated reports, firmware updates and 7-day support; it is explicitly not a cellular fee, and the hub is a separate hardware item that covers up to 50 sensors within about 500 feet

LeakSense bundles hardware and installation into the per-unit fee, but free installation only applies to accessible copper/PEX without pipe rerouting; remote valve control, shutoff valves and tenant billing are gated to higher tiers
YouTilitics charges setup separately ($349) and then a platform fee plus per-device fee, so cost scales with sensor count rather than building count; API/webhooks and unlimited users are included
Parker Plumbing bundles hub, sensors, wiring, startup and monthly reports into the monthly fee but prices installation separately, and boiler testing is an add-on

Moen's subscription adds a continuous limited warranty, support and up to $5,000 in insurance deductible coverage; installation is by independent third-party plumbers and is priced by pipe size, with pipe modifications extra

Leak Shield separates equipment, licensed plumbing, licensed electrical and programming into line items, then bills monitoring annually; live-agent verification, daily plumbing check-ups and plumber dispatch are part of the monthly fee
Monnit's free tier covers basic configuration and email alerts with 100 sensors, but SMS alerts and voice calls cost extra, and Premiere ($45/yr) is what unlocks API access and automated reporting
ProSentry's fee covers design, dashboard, alerts and live operator calls, but sensors are bought per unit at $60-$80 each, so total cost depends on how many sensors each apartment or zone gets
Symmons' $30/sensor/month includes a dedicated cellular network, battery backup and enterprise support - the cellular path is the reason it costs more than Wi-Fi point sensors
Phyn includes pre-freeze warnings and multi-property monitoring (up to 6 properties) at no subscription cost, but there is no property-management or work-order integration published

buyer_complaints.complaint: Flo by Moen users report false 'fast flow' and micro-leak alerts during ordinary use (showers, irrigation, several fixtures), sometimes followed by an unwanted shutoff, plus app/connectivity frustration
Moen is transitioning users to a new app, and its FAQ says the old app's remote-control features stop working after November 1, 2026 - a reminder that app-dependent systems can change under the buyer
A property-management discussion describes flow-monitor alerts triggered by residents turning water on and off, generating unnecessary emergency maintenance callouts

YoLink users report sensors going offline together (attributed by support to a cloud issue) and, in one case, offline sensors triggering false leak sirens - cheap sensors still need health monitoring and alert-rule testing
A reviewer notes the YoLink sensor has no audible alarm of its own, so detection depends entirely on the hub, app and cloud path
SimpliSafe states it will not request dispatch of emergency services for water alarms - a monitored plan gets an automated call, not a response, which is a real gap for unoccupied commercial space

Buyers of the flow-monitoring vendors named in this brief (Alert Labs, WaterSignal, Kontrol) cannot see a price without a sales conversation, which pushes small buyers toward published-price DIY hardware

price_ranges.low_cost_self_serve: $19.99-$105 per sensor plus $0-$45/year software; $0-$30/month per sensor for hosted monitoring (YoLink $19.99 sensor/$23.59 hub/$69.99 kit; FireAvert $40 leak detector, $50 temp/humidity, $60/year monitoring; Monnit $105 sensor, free or $45/yr software; SimpliSafe $19.99 sensor plus 76 cents/day; Phyn $579.99 device with no subscription)
price_ranges.mid_market: $4-$30 per unit, tenant or sensor per month with hardware often included or $40-$80 per point (LeakSense $6-$14/unit/month; Symmons $30/sensor/month; ProSentry $4-$9/tenant/month plus $60-$80 sensors; YouTilitics $20/month platform plus $5/device; SmartRent $18/unit/month bundle)
price_ranges.full_service_or_custom: $99-$399 per building per month for monitored service, with $349-$1,616 setup; $10,000-$12,000 capital for a 100-unit/500-sensor building and about $2/sensor/month monitoring at the low end; $85,000 for about 1,200 sensors at the high end (Parker $149-$399/month; Leak Shield $99/month plus $1,616 install; YouTilitics $349 setup; Habitat-reported $10k-$12k and $2/sensor/month; reported $85k NYC co-op)
price_ranges.inference_note: Ranges are the low and high published figures actually seen in each tier, not averages I computed. Low-cost tier uses only vendor-published hardware and software prices. Mid-market uses per-unit/per-tenant subscriptions with published numbers. Full-service mixes vendor monthly plans (Parker, Leak Shield) with buyer-reported capital and monitoring figures from Habitat Magazine and a Better Buildings case study, so it is broader and less precise. Where a vendor publishes nothing (Alert Labs, WaterSignal, Kontrol), no number was invented; historic third-party figures are shown separately and labeled.

implications_for_consultancy: Inference: the realistic competitive set is the installer-led monthly tier ($149-$399/building/month plus installation), not DIY sensors. Reasoning: Parker bundles hub, sensors, wiring, monthly reports and startup for $149-$399, and Leak Shield charges $99/month with a $1,616 install, so a local firm quoting in that band is pricing against an established, published alternative rather than against a $20 sensor.

Inference: setup fees of $349-$1,616 are already normalized in this market. Reasoning: YouTilitics charges $349 for gateway setup and onboarding, Leak Shield itemizes $1,616 for a single valve-plus-two-sensors install, and ProSentry charges $60-$80 per sensor. A $500-$1,500 integration/setup fee for a 20-60 point building is inside the observed range and should be itemized (hardware, labor, programming) the way Leak Shield does it.

Inference: price monitoring per monitored point with a platform floor, not per building. Reasoning: every published commercial plan except Parker's flat tiers is per unit, per tenant, per sensor or per device ($4-$30), and small commercial buildings around Middlesex County will have 10-60 points; a $150-$300/month floor plus $3-$8 per point maps onto the range buyers already see and protects margin as sensor counts grow.

Inference: hardware markup is not defensible, service is. Reasoning: sensor prices are public and low (YoLink $19.99, FireAvert $40, Monnit $105, SimpliSafe $19.99), so pass hardware through near cost and earn on installation labor, programming, integration and the monthly retainer. Leak Shield's own breakdown (valve $619, sensors $198, plumbing $300, electrical $300, programming $199) is a template for transparent, defensible line items.

Inference: the defensible premium is response and integration, not detection. Reasoning: SimpliSafe explicitly will not dispatch for water alarms, YoLink sensors can go offline and have no local audible alarm, and Flo owners report false alerts and unwanted shutoffs. A retainer that includes alert triage, after-hours escalation to a named person, sensor-health checks, quarterly testing and tuning, plus work-order/PM-system integration, answers the documented complaints and justifies $250-$500/month for a 20-50 point building.

Inference: boiler and freeze coverage is the under-priced wedge for New Jersey. Reasoning: only Parker and FireAvert publish hardware that addresses boiler/heating and freeze risk in this set (Parker lists heating-system monitoring as a plan feature and boiler testing as an add-on; FireAvert sells a $50 temp/humidity sensor), while consumer devices only offer pre-freeze warnings. A combined leak + low-temperature + boiler-room offering aimed at 5-200 staff owners of older Milltown-area buildings is priced against less direct competition than pure leak detection.

Inference: avoid 36-month commitments. Reasoning: Moen's Leak Protection Service requires 36 months with a 50% remaining-payments cancellation fee, while LeakSense, YouTilitics and FireAvert are monthly or annual. Offering month-to-month with a discounted annual option is a low-cost differentiator for a small local firm and lowers the buyer's approval hurdle.

Inference: sell against the claim, not the subscription. Reasoning: FireAvert cites a national average water claim around $11,500 and up to $22,000 in its own portfolio; an annual $3,000-$6,000 retainer is a fraction of one claim, so proposals should lead with the buyer's deductible and insurance-renewal exposure rather than per-sensor price comparisons against YoLink.

Inference: buyers will compare against free-software products, so never sell software access alone. Reasoning: Phyn charges $0 in subscription and Monnit's Basic tier is always free; the paid value has to be installation, commissioning, escalation and reporting, which is what Parker and Leak Shield actually charge for.
caveats: All prices retrieved 2026-11-12 unless a source is dated. Historic figures are labeled with their year.

Several vendor storefronts (Moen/Flo, Phyn, YoLink, SimpliSafe, ProSentry) render prices with script, so the numbers were captured from search-engine renderings of those same URLs rather than from the fetched HTML. They are vendor figures but should be re-checked on the live page before quoting.

The ProSentry $4-$9/tenant and $60-$80/sensor figures come from a search-rendered summary of the vendor's own FAQ; the fetched FAQ body did not contain the price block. GlobeSt (April 2025) separately reported $50-$90 per sensor.
SmartRent's $18/unit/month is a 2024 promotional package price from a vendor social post that bundles two leak sensors with a deadbolt, hub and software - it is not a leak-monitoring list price.
WaterSignal's $50/building/month comes from an undated WaterWorld trade article, not from WaterSignal's current price list; WaterSignal, Alert Labs and Kontrol Technologies publish no current prices.

No New Jersey or Middlesex County provider with a published monitoring price was found. FSC Leak Detection is New Jersey-based and advertises commercial leak monitoring but publishes no prices; Parker Plumbing serves the Hudson Valley in New York and was used as the nearest published installer-led comparison.
Buyer-reported totals (Habitat, Better Buildings, Phantom H2O) are reported, not verified invoices, and cover multifamily buildings much larger than a typical 5-200 staff local business.
Prices exclude sales tax, permits, electrician work outside the quoted scope, and any building Wi-Fi or network upgrades.
Multi-year discounts and volume tiers exist (FireAvert bulk pricing, Leak Shield volume pricing, LeakSense enterprise) but are not published, so they are not reflected in the ranges.
The Mercy Housing and NYC co-op figures were not confirmed on the primary page (PDF fetch failed; podcast page returned only show notes), so they are treated as second-hand.
data_gaps: No published Alert Labs list price for Flowie O, Floodie, Shuttie or Sensor Relay, and no public cancellation or refund terms - only an annual-renewal confirmation.
No published WaterSignal current price, contract term or what the monitoring fee includes.
Kontrol Technologies publishes no pricing for its water leak detection and monitoring.
ADT's water and temperature sensor has no public per-sensor price, and its PowerG water sensor requires a technician visit with no published installation fee.
No New Jersey-specific published monitoring prices or invoices were found for leak, freeze or boiler monitoring; a local quote survey would be needed to confirm Middlesex County rates.
Boiler-specific monitoring is rarely priced as its own line item; Parker treats heating-system monitoring as part of a plan and boiler testing as an add-on without a price.
No public data on multi-year contract discounts, price escalation at renewal, or sensor replacement/battery costs inside monitoring plans.
SimpliSafe's water sensor price and plan dollar equivalents were captured from script-rendered pages/search renderings; the plans themselves are published per day, not per month.
